## Summary

- Adds `gdoc toc <DOC>` command that extracts headings from a Google Doc and outputs a markdown TOC with clickable deep links (`https://docs.google.com/document/d/ID/edit#heading=HEADING_ID`)
- New API function `get_document_headings()` in `api/docs.py` walks `body.content` to extract heading level, ID, and text
- Supports `--tab` (target a specific tab, appends `&tab=t.ID` to links), `--max-depth N` (filter by heading level), `--no-links` (plain text outline)
- All four output modes: terse (default markdown TOC), plain (TSV), json, verbose (with count)
- 18 new tests covering all flags, output modes, tab support, awareness system integration, and the API-layer extraction logic

## Motivation

Getting deep links to specific sections in a Google Doc is a common need (e.g., for sharing in Slack, linking from READMEs, building navigation). The Docs API exposes `headingId` on paragraph styles, but there's no convenient way to extract these from the CLI. This closes that gap.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_toc.py -v` — all 18 tests pass
- [x] Full suite (`uv run python -m pytest tests/ -v`) — all 807 tests pass
- [x] `uv run ruff check` — no new lint issues
- [ ] Manual test: `gdoc toc <real-doc-url>` produces correct markdown links that open to the right heading
